sections.title: Identification and form
sections.text: This entry represents Quercus petraea, sessile oak, a deciduous tree of dry to moist woodland. It usually reaches 18–30 m and can approach 40 m.

sections.title: Leaves and acorns
sections.text: The leaves are about 8–12 cm long, sometimes longer, and have a distinct petiole. The acorns are sessile or nearly so. Unlike Q. robur, sessile oak has acorns without a long stalk, while its leaves have a more noticeable petiole.

sections.title: Identification and edibility
sections.text: Intermediate forms and hybridisation can complicate distinction from Q. robur. The sources consulted do not describe an acorn food preparation here; do not eat them raw.
